pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:741 The MCP capability vocabulary has two hand-maintained authorities: the advertised tool list in `server_tools` and this dispatch match. `scripts/ci/mcp-gate-parity.mjs` only checks that the gated subset is spelled the same at three sites; the vocabulary is still not rendered from one registry.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:741 The dispatch arms are written separately from the json! tool definitions in server_tools (line 167). The static `instructions` doctrine at line 150 also names tools such as enqueue_job and approve_transaction, and no sync check resolves those mentions against what is actually listed.

pairs.evidence: scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:314 The hook only writes a fixed reminder to stderr, and the external Claude Code harness decides where that text lands in the model's context. Searching scripts/docs found no system prompt, token budget, cache-control or compaction code, so this context owns no prompt assembler.

pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/apps/provisioner/src/lib.rs:1016 Provisioner, research and connector-api-watch each build model-facing prose with inline format! calls inside run() or a helper, so no single assembler enforces section order, trust classification, a total budget or a fingerprint.

techniques.evidence: crates/apps/provisioner/src/lib.rs:1016 Prompt text is born at the call site in run(); there is no assembler per prompt family. This is the sprawl failure.
crates/apps/provisioner/src/lib.rs:1144 An untrusted scraped page body is interpolated straight into the task text, with no declared trust class and no fenced insertion point.

crates/apps/connector-api-watch/src/lib.rs:443 clamp() silently drops diff lines past the cap, and the prompt never says how many ADDED/REMOVED lines were omitted, so the model sees a partial view that looks complete.
crates/apps/research/src/lib.rs:612 The task layer opens with role priming. It does carry a done criterion (the JSON shape), but the opening line is spent on a role claim.

crates/apps/research/src/lib.rs:633 This is the agent-held regime: the Claude CLI session holds the transcript and the app sends only a delta prompt, with no client-side compaction running in parallel.
